evals.name: Progressing inside the progress deadline is not 'still working'
evals.prompt: An automated check fired because Application payments in team-frontend has been Progressing for 4 minutes. The health message is 'Waiting for rollout to finish: 0 of 3 updated replicas are available...'. Is this still rolling out normally, or is something wrong?
expectations: Does not conclude that the Application is fine merely because the status is Progressing rather than Degraded

States that a Deployment stays Progressing until its Progressing condition reaches ProgressDeadlineExceeded, and that progressDeadlineSeconds defaults to 600 seconds, so a 4-minute-old failure is indistinguishable from a healthy rollout at the Application level
Inspects the pods behind the Deployment — phase, container waiting reason, restart count, previous termination — rather than reasoning from the Application status alone
States what evidence would distinguish wedged from still working, such as whether replica counts or the health lastTransitionTime have moved

evals.name: Unknown masks a real fault
evals.prompt: Application checkout reports health Unknown. The health message on resource widgets.example.com/Widget is 'attempt to index a nil value (field status)'. The team says their Deployment is also crash looping. What is the root cause?
expectations: Identifies the message as an error from a custom Lua health script, and the status as a failure to compute health rather than a failure of the workload
States that Unknown is the worst status in the rollup order, so it masks the crash-looping Deployment, which is why the Application does not report Degraded
Points at resource.customizations.health.<group>_<Kind> in argocd-cm as where the script lives, and locates the fix there rather than in the workload
Re-checks the remaining resources and reports the crash-looping Deployment as a second, masked finding rather than merging it into the Unknown
Does not claim the Widget CR itself is unhealthy on the strength of the Unknown status

evals.name: A missing ConfigMap does not make an Application Missing
evals.prompt: Application reports health Missing. Someone deleted a ConfigMap that the app's Deployment mounts. Is the deleted ConfigMap why the Application health is Missing?
expectations: States that it is not, because a missing resource only affects Application health when Argo CD can health-assess its kind, and there is no built-in or bundled health check for ConfigMap
Directs the investigation to a resource of a kind that does have a health assessment — such as Deployment, StatefulSet, Service, PVC, Job, Ingress, or a CRD with a bundled or custom Lua script
May note that the deleted ConfigMap can still cause a Degraded workload, for example CreateContainerConfigError, without being the source of the Missing status
Does not assert that any deleted resource makes an Application Missing

evals.name: Degraded and Synced at the same time
evals.prompt: Application api is Degraded and Synced. The Deployment health message says it exceeded its progress deadline and the pods are in CrashLoopBackOff with a non-zero exit code. The team wants to know whether to re-sync or hard refresh.
expectations: States that Synced means live state already matches git, so drift is not the cause and re-syncing or refreshing will not change the outcome
Treats 'exceeded its progress deadline' as a timeout rather than a root cause, and goes to the pods for the actual failure
Uses the previous container's logs for a crash loop, noting that the current container has not failed yet
Names a specific cause supported by the evidence, rather than listing possibilities

evals.name: Pending deletion
evals.prompt: Application platform has been Progressing for 40 minutes. The only non-healthy resource shows health message 'Pending deletion'. What is happening and what should be done?
expectations: States that a resource with a deletionTimestamp and no hook finalizer is reported Progressing with that message regardless of anything else
Checks metadata.finalizers on the object, and the namespace phase and finalizers, as the thing blocking deletion
Identifies this as a controller not removing its finalizer, not an Argo CD fault, and says that syncing or refreshing will not clear it
Does not recommend re-syncing the Application as the fix

evals.name: No action required
evals.prompt: Automated diagnosis fired on Application data-migration, Progressing for 12 minutes. The only progressing resource is a Job whose pod is Running, restartPolicy OnFailure, writing new log lines, and the job normally takes 30 minutes. Produce a diagnosis.
expectations: States that a Job with no Complete or Failed condition is reported Progressing, and that a pod with restartPolicy OnFailure or Never is Progressing while Running rather than Healthy, so both are expected here
Concludes that no action is required and returns a diagnosis without a remediation, rather than inventing a fix for a healthy long-running job
Supports the conclusion with observed progress, such as advancing log output or a recent health lastTransitionTime
Does not recommend deleting, restarting, or re-syncing the Job

evals.name: Self-heal makes a cluster-side fix wrong
evals.prompt: Application web is Degraded. The container is in ImagePullBackOff because the image tag in the manifests is wrong. spec.syncPolicy.automated.selfHeal is true. Give me the command to fix it.
expectations: States that the cause is in the manifests, so the correction belongs in git
States that with selfHeal true a manual cluster-side change such as kubectl set image is reverted by Argo CD within seconds, so it is not a fix
Does not supply a kubectl or oc command that mutates the live Deployment as the answer
Reports the wrong tag as the root cause, with the ImagePullBackOff reason or event text as the supporting evidence

evals.name: Hook pod failure does not surface as unhealthy
evals.prompt: Application billing shows health Missing and the sync operation phase is Failed. A PreSync hook pod is in ImagePullBackOff, but no resource in the Application shows as Degraded. Why is nothing Degraded, and what is the root cause?
expectations: States that hooks are excluded from the Application health rollup, which is why the failing hook pod does not appear as a Degraded resource
Adds that a pod with restartPolicy OnFailure or Never does not take the waiting-reason Degraded path at all, by design, so hook pods are not failed prematurely
Identifies the failed PreSync hook as the reason the sync never reached the resources, making the missing resources a symptom rather than a separate finding
Reports one root cause — the hook image cannot be pulled — rather than reporting the missing resources as an independent problem
